binary_io.note: The sources name four binary and serialization formats of documented-only listings (a graph-tool binary, a NetworKit binary, Python pickle, a Thrill graph binary) and give no checkable specification of any of them.

text_edge_list_io.note: The sources list edge-list, adjacency-list, CSV, KONECT, LGL, METIS, NCOL and SNAP text readers and writers by name only (documented tools, never run); no specification of any of these formats is among the sources.

graph_markup_io.note: The format grammars (GEXF, GML, GraphML, Pajek, node-link JSON) are specified in documents not read for this survey; only the round-trip property that was compared is stated. DIMACS, GRAPH6, GRAPHDB, GRAPHVIZ, LEDA, LEMON, NODELINKJSON, SVG and TSPLIB are listed by documented tools and are not specified in the sources.

notation.meaning: the features format \(f\) can store: node identifiers, edge endpoints with direction, edge weights, node attributes
equality of two networks on the features in \(\mathrm{carry}(f)\): same node identifiers, same multiset of directed edges, same weights and attributes

formulas.name: Round-trip property compared in this survey
formulas.where: A format is read and written correctly when reading the written file returns a network equal to the original on every feature the format can carry. This is the property checked, in both directions between tools; it is not a published formula of a format. A format that cannot store a feature (attributes in Pajek, a double quote inside a Pajek label) is checked only on what it can carry.

matrix_file_io.note: The sources list matrix and spreadsheet readers and writers (UCINET DL and binary datasets, MATLAB, MATRIX, Matrix Market, MTX, RB, XLSX) by name only; no specification of these formats is among the sources, and the UCINET entries are documented, never run.

partition_cover_io.note: The sources list five partition and cover file formats of one documented tool by name only; none is specified in the sources.
